facts.text: On this date in 1305, William Wallace was executed in London — yet Scotland's population today is smaller than it was in 1851, when 2.9 million people lived there before emigration hollowed out the Highlands.

On August 23, 1939, the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact secretly divided Europe between Hitler and Stalin — the two countries sharing that border today, Lithuania and Latvia, were erased from maps for 50 years as a direct result.
Manila is the most densely populated city on Earth, packing over 70,000 people per square kilometer — denser than any neighborhood in Tokyo, New York, or Mumbai.
More people live inside a 4,000 km radius of Dhaka, Bangladesh than exist in the entire Western Hemisphere.
Indonesia has more volcanoes than any other country — 139 active ones — and roughly 8.6 million people live within the immediate danger zones of eruption.

On this day in 1907, Panic gripped Wall Street as the Knickerbocker Trust collapsed, triggering a crisis so severe that J.P. Morgan personally corralled bankers in his library and locked the door until they agreed to bail out the system.
On August 23, 1973, hostages taken in a Stockholm bank robbery began defending their captors to police — giving psychiatry the term 'Stockholm syndrome' and finance an unlikely origin story.
The New York Stock Exchange was founded under a buttonwood tree in 1792 with just 24 brokers and five securities. It is now the world's largest exchange by market cap, at roughly $25 trillion.

Berkshire Hathaway was originally a failing textile company. Warren Buffett later called buying it the worst trade of his life — a mistake that still compounded into the world's most famous conglomerate.

The Dutch East India Company, the first publicly traded corporation, was so large at its 17th-century peak that its inflation-adjusted value exceeded the combined worth of Apple, Microsoft, and Amazon today.
On this date in 1966, Lunar Orbiter 1 captured the first photograph of Earth from the Moon's vicinity — a pale crescent hanging in black nothing, 40 years before smartphones existed.
On August 23, 2003, Mars made its closest approach to Earth in 60,000 years, near enough that a backyard telescope revealed its polar ice caps.
Your skeleton is not static infrastructure. Almost every atom in your bones is replaced within a decade, meaning the skeleton you were born with is long gone.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere roughly the size of a city. A teaspoon of its material would weigh about a billion tons on Earth.
Sharks are older than trees. Sharks evolved roughly 450 million years ago; forests didn't appear until about 385 million years ago.

On this day in 1939, Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union signed the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact — stunning the world by turning sworn ideological enemies into allies overnight, and sealing Poland's fate within days.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded. Europe's oldest university predates what we call 'ancient' Mesoamerican civilization by three centuries.
On this day in 1305, William Wallace was executed in London. Braveheart's hero died before the printing press, before Columbus, and before the Black Death — medieval in ways most films never convey.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She was as remote from the pyramid's builders as we are from Julius Caesar.
The fax machine was invented in 1843 — 33 years before Alexander Graham Bell patented the telephone. Sending documents remotely is older than voice calls.

**Sonder** (n.) — the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in *The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows* (2012), it spread so fast linguists now track it as a genuine neologism.
**Hiraeth** (Welsh, n.) — a longing for a home you cannot return to, or perhaps never had. Untranslatable into English, it carries grief, nostalgia, and belonging folded into a single breath.

**Petrichor** (n.) — the smell of rain on dry earth. Named on this date in 1964 when Australian scientists Isabel Joy Bear and R.G. Thomas published the word in *Nature*, fusing Greek *petra* (stone) and *ichor* (the fluid in gods' veins).

**Saudade** (Portuguese, n.) — a melancholic longing for something beloved and absent. Emperor Charles V reportedly called Portuguese *the language of saudade*, considering it untranslatable — a claim the Portuguese have happily never corrected.

On August 23, 1305, William Wallace was executed in London. The Scots word **dreich** — meaning bleak, grey, dreary weather — likely described that day exactly as it describes Scottish skies today: a one-syllable verdict on the sky.

On this date in 2012, Coinbase processed its first bitcoin sale — $13.61 worth — marking the debut of the company that would eventually custody more BTC than any entity outside the Satoshi wallet cluster.
On this date in 2017, Bitcoin's SegWit upgrade activated on mainnet after a two-year civil war, separating transaction signatures from block data and doubling effective capacity without a hard fork.
The Ethereum genesis block, mined in July 2015, contained a hidden message in its extra data field: a Times headline — the same journalistic ritual Satoshi used in Bitcoin's block zero.

Bitcoin's difficulty adjustment recalculates every 2,016 blocks — chosen because it equals exactly two weeks at 10-minute intervals, giving miners a predictable reorg window without central coordination.

The DAO hack of 2016 drained 3.6 million ETH through a single reentrancy bug, but the attacker was legally unable to move the funds for 28 days due to the contract's own withdrawal lock — time enough for Ethereum to hard-fork them back.

On this date in 2012, the 'Google Brain' cat neuron paper by Le et al. was submitted to arXiv—a network of 16,000 CPU cores trained unsupervised to recognize cats, igniting the modern large-scale deep learning era.

On this date in 2011, Siri launched in beta as a standalone app before Apple acquired and embedded it in the iPhone 4S, meaning the world's first mainstream AI assistant existed briefly as a third-party download.
GPT-4's training compute is estimated at around 2×10²⁵ FLOPs—roughly 100 million times more than AlexNet in 2012, a scaling factor that took just eleven years.

Transformers were not invented for language. The 2017 'Attention Is All You Need' paper targeted machine translation; the architecture's dominance across vision, audio, and protein folding was entirely unanticipated by its authors.

AlphaFold 2 predicted structures for over 200 million proteins—essentially the entire known proteome—yet the entire database was generated faster than a single experimental crystallography lab could solve 1,000 structures.
